stages.name: International economics: trade effects
stages.title: International economics: trade effects
stages.sub: After this you can explain how trade liberalisation changes outcomes for producers, consumers and markets, and why the WTO exists.

steps.q: A UK car maker can now sell to 500 million EU customers instead of just 65 million UK ones. What happens to the number of cars it can sell?
steps.right: It can sell far more cars
steps.wrong: It can only sell the same amount
steps.hint: Think about how many more customers just became reachable.

steps.q: When tariffs fall, foreign carmakers can sell in the UK more cheaply than before. What starts arriving in UK showrooms?
steps.wrong: Only the same UK brands as before
steps.hint: Lower tariffs make it easier for outsiders to sell here too.

steps.q: With many more brands of car on sale, and each one trying to undercut the others on price, what do UK car buyers notice?
steps.right: More models to pick from and lower prices
steps.hint: More sellers competing for the same buyers usually does what to price and variety?

steps.q: The UK car maker now faces those cheaper foreign brands at home too, not just bigger export markets. To keep customers, what must it do to its cars and factories?
steps.right: Improve them and cut wasted costs
steps.wrong: Keep them exactly the same as before
steps.hint: If it does nothing while rivals undercut it, what happens to its sales?

steps.q: The UK, France and Germany form a bloc with no tariffs between them at all, even lower barriers than global trade rules require. Inside that bloc, do firms face even more rivals pushing them to improve, or fewer?
steps.right: Even more rivals, so more pressure to improve
steps.wrong: Fewer rivals, so less pressure to improve
steps.hint: A tighter regional deal removes even more barriers than exist globally.

steps.q: Two countries disagree over a tariff, and 160 others have agreed shared rules on trade barriers. What kind of body is needed to referee disputes like this and keep barriers falling worldwide?
steps.right: A global organisation that sets and enforces trade rules
steps.wrong: Each country's own courts deciding on their own
steps.hint: Think about who could apply the same rules to every country rather than just one side judging its own case.
